//: Hand-decided half of the rig catalogue. tools/sync-hamlib.mjs --build joins
this with tools/hamlib-sources.json (Hamlib's own rig_caps) to produce
js/connectors/rigs-generated.js.
Hamlib supplies model numbers, names, manufacturers and serial defaults. It
cannot supply the CAT byte protocol — that is C code per backend, not data —
so every rig needs a WebHam protocol family assigned here before it can be
emitted. An unmapped rig is reported, never guessed: a name in the picker
that fails on connect is worse than an absent one.
EVERYTHING IS KEYED BY HAMLIB'S RIG_MODEL_* TOKEN, NOT BY MODEL NUMBER.
WebHam's hand-written catalogue and Hamlib disagree about which rig owns
which number for 22 models (WebHam's 1024 is the FT-817ND; Hamlib's 1024 is
the FT-1000MP). Keying on the number would pair one rig's protocol family
with another rig's name and serial settings — wrong CAT bytes to a real
radio. The token is stable identity; the number is derived from it.
Why families are per-model and not per-backend: Hamlib's `yaesu` backend
spans both the 5-byte binary rigs (FT-817/857/897) and the newcat ASCII ones
(FT-450/950/991/DX10), and its `kenwood` backend contains Elecraft and
PowerSDR too. Hamlib has no notion of WebHam's classic-vs-modern split, so
that judgement lives here.

backendFamilies.//: Fallback when a model has no explicit entry below. Empty on purpose: a family assignment decides which bytes go down the wire, so it should always be a reviewed per-model decision rather than a backend-wide guess.

//RIG_MODEL_DELTAII: Was kenwood-ascii, which could not have worked. Ten-Tec licensed Icom's CI-V for
the Delta II: Hamlib implements it in rigs/icom/delta2.c with a full
icom_priv_caps (CI-V address 0x01, civ_731_mode on) and a 1200-baud-only serial
line. As kenwood-ascii, WebHam sent `FA00014074000;` ASCII at 19200 to a radio
that speaks CI-V binary at 1200. Caught by the civFamilies check below.

//civFamilies: Which WebHam families speak Icom CI-V. Used by --build to check that every rig
Hamlib gives icom_priv_caps for is mapped to one of them — a CI-V radio pointed at
an ASCII family is a profile that cannot work, and the per-rig CI-V address would
be emitted onto a profile with no way to use it.
Kept here rather than in the tool because it is a fact about WebHam's families,
i.e. a hand-decided mapping, which is what this file is for.

//RIG_MODEL_DELTAII: Hamlib gives this rig serial_rate_min == serial_rate_max == 1200, so 1200 is not a
preference, it is the only rate the radio accepts. icom-civ-classic's family default
of 19200 is outside that range, which --diff reported as serial/3064/baudRate.

nameOverrides.//: Keyed by RIG_MODEL_* token. Empty: the generated catalogue uses Hamlib's own "<mfg> <model_name>" so labels track upstream. Add an entry only to override a specific label.

allowNonSerial.//: Tokens to emit even though Hamlib marks them non-serial, because a vendor virtual COM port makes them reachable from Web Serial (SmartSDR CAT, PowerSDR).

exclude.//: Hamlib model tokens deliberately not offered.

//: Profiles WebHam defines itself, emitted alongside the Hamlib-derived ones.
Their ids are namespaced `wh:<slug>` rather than numeric ON PURPOSE. Now that
the catalogue adopts Hamlib model numbers, a WebHam-only profile keeping its
old number would sooner or later sit on a real Hamlib model: four already did
(FT-980 on Hamlib's 1013=FT-900, FT-817ND on 1024=FT-1000MP, FTDX-9000Contest
on 1032=FTDX-5000, TS-60S on 2016=TS-570S). The FT-817ND case is the sharp
one — it is yaesu-5byte binary CAT while Hamlib's 1024 is ASCII, so a stale
saved id would have driven a radio with another radio's protocol.
`group` records why each is here (see `unresolvedNotes` below); `wasId` is the
pre-migration numeric id, kept so the migration table stays auditable.
old profileId -> new profileId, applied once to localStorage
(web-ham-logger.cat-settings.profile, and the .overrides blob's own
profileId field) by js/connectors/cat.js on load.
Covers every id the hand-written catalogue shipped that changes:
- 22 rigs whose number disagreed with Hamlib and are now renumbered to it
- 27 WebHam-only profiles moved to namespaced `wh:` ids
Ids absent from this table are unchanged (they already agreed with Hamlib).
Without this, adopting Hamlib numbering silently repoints a saved profile at
a different radio — in several cases a different protocol family and baud
rate, i.e. the wrong bytes to real hardware.

needs a human decision, and several look like pre-existing bugs.
naming-variant  almost certainly IS in Hamlib under a different spelling
(FT-991A vs FT991A, IC-910H vs IC910). Needs an alias.
unsupported     the rig's Hamlib backend (AOR, JRC, Ten-Tec, Alinco,
Barrett) has no WebHam protocol implementation. All 14 are
currently mapped to kenwood-ascii in cat.js, which an AOR
AR8600 does not speak — these very likely do not work
today and should be dropped or given a real protocol.
